## Emergence of functional organisation in developing cortex

How do orientation maps and other functional structures arise before and
around eye opening? I use recurrent network models to ask which features of
early cortical circuits are sufficient to produce the structure seen in
spontaneous and evoked activity.

## Variability and learning in recurrent networks

Trial-to-trial variability is often treated as noise. In developing circuits
it may instead reflect the state of a network that is still being shaped.
This line of work asks how variability changes with learning in
two-dimensional recurrent networks.

## Cross-species comparison

Comparing cortical organisation across species, for example ferret, cat and
tree shrew, constrains which developmental mechanisms are general and which
are specific.
